## Result

- Skill: design-review.
- Review status: approved.
- Review ID: design-review-r8.
- Exact package: seven living models (Design, System, Workflow, Review and Closeout, Record Format, CLI, Test) plus retained Target-native init.
- Supporting consumer: boundary-first-proof-model adopted model-format reference.
- Direction: unchanged bounded proposal plus explicit user request to rename the document marker and show an example.
- Material findings / required correction: none.
- Next owner: Route and independently reviewed Delivery; no implementation, runtime-validator success, candidate support, Verify or PR claim.

## Independent engineering judgment

The rename is a document-contract change owned by DES-SR-11. It selects exactly model-document-v1, retires the ambiguous old document identifier without a dual alias, and preserves the existing table/reference/path/fence grammar. The seven current model declarations and version-domain explanations agree. The retained TNI feature boundary marker and all stored/runtime/transport format meanings remain unchanged. RF-SR-06 still retires old stored formats; targeted-recording-v1 remains a separate request interface. This is neither a stored-schema migration nor a new lifecycle gate.

The transition explicitly coordinates documents, validator, authoring resource/skeleton and generated candidate metadata. Existing customer documents require an explicitly authorized owner edit; installation never silently rewrites them. The old marker and unknown/missing/duplicate declarations reject before table checks. Rollback restores a coherent document/validator/guidance set without restoring retired runtime readers. Those choices make the break understandable and bounded, and preserve exact prior reviewed subjects rather than relabeling them.

The boundary-first-proof-model edit is an adopted-profile owner/reference update for this Design-owned marker, not a substantive amendment to retained feature serialization or its PBF requirements. It does not require converting the historical feature contract. Other model changes are document-marker/explanation changes; their local behavioral/assessment/runtime requirements retain meaning. The eight-member package includes relevant owners and retained installer basis without claiming an installation-model migration.

## Example assessment

The inline indexed label-normalization example is explicitly a complete illustrative structural record at a hypothetical model path, not a deployed RigorLoop component, runtime record or promise of a complete technical design for every concern. Its index names DES-SR-09/11/12, purpose, scope and synthetic LAB identities. Its three local requirements define ASCII-space trimming while preserving interior characters, rejection of non-string input with no value, and purity/idempotence. The concrete quoted input/output and empty/non-string conditions agree with those obligations.

All eight dimensions are present once. Applicable rows reference declared local requirements and observable conditions; identity/authority and persisted compatibility are explicitly non-applicable for this pure transformation, with caller ownership and reasons. State and retry scenarios do not invent persistence or permission rules; failure leaves state unchanged, and locale does not alter the ASCII rule. These are representative conditions, not an exhaustive test whitelist or actual execution evidence. The example is inside the owning Design, so its exact file identity covers both text and example; its index and final paragraph require renewed owner/example assessment when relied upon.

I independently extracted the fenced text and counted three unique LAB requirements, eight scenario rows and one marker. Existing parser inspection confirms fenced content is omitted from the parent structural scan. Calling the existing validator on both actual new-marker texts correctly returns BFR-MODEL-CONTRACT because implementation has not changed. Replacing only the marker in memory with the old accepted spelling yields no structural issue for either parent or extracted example. This is bounded feasibility evidence that unchanged grammar works; it is not a passing validation claim for the prospective marker or permission to keep accepting its retired spelling.

## Prior basis, independence and limits

The complete earlier package reasoning remains applicable except the explicitly assessed marker/consumer/example delta. No material product direction, RC policy, runtime record semantics or installer safety is weakened. Original reviews/records and the thirteen historical installer prose errors remain unchanged. Actual new-marker dispatch, invalid-marker negatives and rebuilt installed/candidate outcomes remain M3 proof obligations before implementation review and final closeout.

Concrete independent nonauthor /root/independent_design_review assessed the user-requested marker rename and illustrative example plus complete affected Design and Delivery packages. Primary-agent authored all governed model/plan changes; reviewer performed read-only semantic/structural feasibility checks and authored only these reviews. Passing author checks and prior approvals do not substitute for this assessment.
